trust_decision.summary: pbxapi trusts any HS256 JWT whose signature verifies against JWT_KEY, which is a string literal in the shipped source; the key is set in pbxapi/index.php and checked in models/authorize.php (all REST/manager controllers) and models/jwtauth.php (refresh).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'hard-coded JWT key'. Grepping for JWT_KEY lands on the literal at once, and it is the only place the key is defined.

fix_sites.entry_point: any HTTP request to /pbxapi/* (f3 routes /@controller, /@controller/@id at index.php:50-55): load /etc/issabel.conf and fail closed when pbxapijwtsecret is missing, invalid Base64 or under 32 bytes (fix.diff:13-32)
same bootstrap; JWT_KEY is consumed by POST /pbxapi/authenticate (sign), GET /pbxapi/authenticate/@id (refresh: verify+sign) and every controller via authorize->authorized (verify) (fix.diff:39-40)
same bootstrap; parse_conf is rewritten to split on the first '=' only and to skip comments and blank lines, so Base64 '=' padding survives (fix.diff:46-73)
fix_sites.module_kind: config parser (helper in the same file)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only framework/html/pbxapi/index.php. The nearest out-of-module site is the RPM %post key substitution at issabel-framework.spec:253-255 (and the copy at build/4.0/issabel-framework.spec:249-250), which the fix did not change; it is recorded under O8.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The RPM spec is packaging, not application code, and it already 'randomizes' the key at install time (issabel-framework.spec:253-255), so a solver can argue the literal is only a placeholder and key provisioning is out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The web UI login fetches a pbxapi token server-side through curl POST /pbxapi/authenticate with the admin user and amiadminpwd. It stores the token in the PHP session, and GET /pbxapi/authenticate hands it back. Token refresh through GET /pbxapi/authenticate/@id must keep working when tokens are signed with the configured key. A fix that breaks config parsing (for example amiadminpwd or a secret containing '=') or rejects all tokens breaks UI login.

O6_input_shapes: pbxapijwtsecret decoding to fewer than 32 bytes (fix.diff:30-31)
config values containing '=' such as Base64 padding (explode limit 2, fix.diff:64)
comment lines starting with '#' or ';' and blank lines (fix.diff:60-62)

O7_producer.where: framework/html/pbxapi/index.php:59-67 (parse_conf); duplicate parser at framework/html/pbxapi/models/jwtauth.php:60-68, which the fix did not change and which reads amiadminpwd for the login check at jwtauth.php:164

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Key provisioning: the RPM %post 'random' key is an RPM %(...) macro, expanded once at package build time and seeded from date +%s. Every install of one RPM therefore shares a predictable key. The fix moves the key to /etc/issabel.conf, but nothing at the pinned commit writes pbxapijwtsecret.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Packaging/build script rather than PHP; it looks like it already randomizes the key; the advisory names pbxapi only.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: repo root spec file vs framework/html/pbxapi/index.php; different language (RPM/shell)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Legacy 4.0 build spec with the same build-time %(...) key substitution
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Legacy build directory for an older release.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A post-install helper that appends pbxapijwtsecret=<value> to /etc/issabel.conf using a weak or fixed fallback (as it already does with amiadminpwd 'issabel789' at line 87)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This script already provisions amiadminpwd into /etc/issabel.conf with a hard-coded default, so a maintainer would naturally add the JWT secret in the same place, in the same style.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: jwtauth's own constructor/parse_conf reads the signing key with a fallback literal when the conf key is missing, so the token issue/refresh path does not use the bootstrap JWT_KEY
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: jwtauth already duplicates parse_conf and reads /etc/issabel.conf on its own, so a second key source here is a natural second implementation, one file away from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: authorize falls back to a default key or accepts the legacy literal during a 'migration' window when JWT_KEY is empty
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Backward compatibility for tokens issued before the key rotation is a plausible maintainer choice, and it gives a solver a 'must keep working' reason to leave it alone.
